title: もう後戻りできないぞ  (No Turning Back Now)

segments.t: Walking through Susukino at night, Muranishi spots magazines sealed in clear plastic wrap so browsers cannot peek inside without buying. When Toshi tells him they sell over a million copies every month, Muranishi drops all hesitation and marches straight toward a shop called Showtime. Listen to the finale of Episode One.
これは何だ？
ビニールに包まれた中身が見えない本だ。
中身を隠して買わせる新しい本なんだよ。
これを考えた人は頭が切れるよな。
これ、月にどのぐらい売れてるんだ？
月に百万冊以上は売れてるらしい。
百万冊！？
トシ、これを仕入れることはできるか？
急に呼び捨てかよ。
まあ、あのショータイムだ。もう後戻りできないぞ。
分かってる。
行ってくる。
Episode One ends with big numbers, sudden familiarity, and the same two-word doorway phrase Muranishi used at home—now with a brand-new meaning.
ビニールに包まれた中身が見えない本だ。

'It is a book wrapped in vinyl so you cannot see the contents.' "Nakami" joins "naka", inside, with "mi", body or substance—meaning the contents inside a package, bag, or book. "Mienai" means cannot be seen.
中身を隠して買わせる新しい本なんだよ。
'It hides what is inside to make people buy it—a new kind of book.' Turning "kau", to buy, into "kawaseru" expresses making or tempting customers to buy, followed by "atarashii", new.
これを考えた人は頭が切れるよな。
'Whoever thought this up is really sharp.' Just like English 'sharp', "atama ga kireru" literally says 'the head cuts cleanly'—praising a clever, quick-witted business mind!
これ、月にどのぐらい売れてるんだ？
'Roughly how many of these sell per month?' Built from "dono", which, plus "gurai", about, "dono gurai" asks 'roughly how much?', handy for prices, distances, and sales totals alike.
月に百万冊以上は売れてるらしい。
'Over a million copies a month, apparently.' Bound books and magazines count with "satsu". Since "man" is ten thousand, one hundred "man"—"hyakuman"—equals one million, and "rashii" adds 'so I hear'.
トシ、これを仕入れることはできるか？
'Toshi, can we stock these?' Store owners use "shiireru" for buying stock to resell, paired with "koto wa dekiru ka", 'is it possible to?'
急に呼び捨てかよ。

'Suddenly calling me by my bare first name, huh?' Big cultural moment: "yobisute" means dropping "san" or "chan" and calling someone by their bare name alone—showing Muranishi just shifted into boss-and-partner mode "kyuu ni", all of a sudden!
もう後戻りできないぞ。
'There is no turning back anymore.' "Atomodori" combines "ato", back, with "modori", returning—so "mou atomodori dekinai" warns 'you cannot turn back now'.
分かってる。
'I know.' Calm, unhurried "wakatteru" drops yesterday's defensive "yo"—now Muranishi means business.
行ってくる。

'I am going in.' Earlier Muranishi used "itte kuru" with his kids at the front door; here, built from "iku", go, and "kuru", come back, those same words launch a whole new life. Now let's listen to the final scene of Episode One from beginning to end.
これは何だ？
ビニールに包まれた中身が見えない本だ。
中身を隠して買わせる新しい本なんだよ。
これを考えた人は頭が切れるよな。
これ、月にどのぐらい売れてるんだ？
月に百万冊以上は売れてるらしい。
百万冊！？
トシ、これを仕入れることはできるか？
急に呼び捨てかよ。
まあ、あのショータイムだ。もう後戻りできないぞ。
分かってる。
行ってくる。

Congratulations on finishing all of Episode One! You learned "nakami" for contents, "atama ga kireru" for a sharp mind, "yobisute" for dropping polite titles, and saw "itte kuru" come full circle. Until Episode Two—see you next time!
また会いましょう。

source.show: 全裸監督 (The Naked Director) S01E01
